user_reviews.Description:
PROUD TO BE OSMANIAN
I am an MBBS student at Osmania Medical College, one of the most reputed and historic medical colleges in Hyderabad. Being a part of this institution is both an honor and a challenge.

From the first day, I realized that this college is not like others -- it demands discipline, consistency, and serious effort. The academic environment is intense, especially in subjects like Anatomy, Physiology, and Biochemistry. The teaching is strong, and the faculty expect us to be well-prepared, particularly for viva and internal exams.

One of the biggest strengths of my college is the clinical exposure through Osmania General Hospital. Seeing real patients and hospital settings motivates me and gives meaning to what I study.

Campus life is a mix of pressure and enjoyment. There is stress due to studies, but also good friendships, group discussions, and memorable experiences. The competition among students pushes me to improve myself every day.

Overall, studying at Osmania Medical College is not easy, but it is shaping me into a responsible and knowledgeable future doctor. I feel proud to be a part of this institution and I know that the training I receive here will prepare me well for my medical career.

user_reviews.Name: Vinay
user_reviews.Description:
They have two different main blocks one is at Chikkadpally and the other one is at RTC X Roads.
I have done my graduation from this college.

Pros:
* Lectures have excellent subject knowledge.
* Fests like Abhiyaan, Annual Day to explore talents.
* RTC X Roads Block has very good infrastructure then Chikkadpally block.
* There will be many events occurring in the campus atleast 2-3 events in a week.
* Library is also available you can even take books to home.
* TSRTC Bus Stop is very near.
* Many cultural events like Traditional day, Sanskrit Literature day, Batukkamma, Hindi Divas day etc., to learn and have fun.
* Indoor and Outdoor sports also available. But for outdoor sports they book external grounds like Victory playground near Chaderghat.

Cons:
* College have very strict regarding attendance, they will force you to maintain 90% attendance but at the end you should maintain above 75%. * If you don't maintain attendance above 90% you are not allowed for placements in few companies, etc.,
* They have strict rules on appearance like ID, formals, no long hairs, clean shave etc.,
* Chikkadpally block does not have good infrastructure.
* There will be many clubs but many are just OK except NSS and NCC.

Tips:
* Maintain good attendance.
* Make sure to clear all backlogs before reaching final year or else you will not be allowed to sit in placements.
* Participate in Freshers, Annual day, Abhiyaan and enjoy your college life.
* Bunk few classes and travel, it will be your sweet memories 😃😜

user_reviews.Name: Rutwik reddy
user_reviews.Description:
I am an ECE student at Vasavi College of Engineering, Hyderabad, and I want to share my honest experience so that future students can make an informed decision before joining.

Before COVID-19, Vasavi College had an excellent reputation for academics, discipline, and placements. However, based on my experience, the standards have declined over the past few years, especially in the Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) department.

The biggest issue is the lack of focus on core ECE skills. Instead of providing industry-relevant training in areas such as VLSI, Embedded Systems, Digital Design, Communication Systems, or PCB Design, students are mainly encouraged to learn general programming languages such as Java and Python. While coding is useful, it should not replace core technical training for ECE students.

Another major concern is the mandatory Technical Skills Program conducted through CCC. Students are required to pay around ₹5,000–₹10,000 for this program. In my experience, the program offered very little practical learning or value for the money spent. Many students felt that they attended sessions without gaining meaningful technical knowledge. Since participation is mandatory, students have no choice but to pay the fees.

When students raised concerns about the quality of this program, we felt that our feedback was not taken seriously. Instead of discussing possible improvements, we were often told that the benefits would become clear during placements.

The internship policy is another major concern. In today's job market, internships are extremely important. However, in my experience, students who secured valuable internships -- including government opportunities such as DRDO -- faced difficulties obtaining attendance permission from the department. This created unnecessary obstacles for students trying to gain real industry experience.

I also feel that communication between students and higher authorities could be improved. Many students feel it is difficult to directly present their concerns to decision-makers, making it challenging to resolve academic and training-related issues.

The campus is well maintained, and many faculty members are supportive and knowledgeable. However, I feel the administration follows very strict rules that sometimes make the college environment feel more like a school than an engineering college. Students are expected to behave responsibly, but they should also be given opportunities to grow independently.

I believe the ECE department should place greater emphasis on:

- Core ECE subjects such as VLSI, Embedded Systems, FPGA, PCB Design, RF, and Communication Systems.
- Encouraging and supporting students who secure internships.
- Improving the quality and transparency of technical skill programs.
- Listening to student feedback and involving students in decisions that directly affect their education.
- Providing more flexibility for students pursuing internships and industry exposure.

My intention is not to discourage anyone from joining Vasavi College of Engineering but to encourage the management to address these concerns. The college has a strong reputation and the potential to be one of the best engineering colleges in Telangana again. I sincerely hope the administration considers student feedback and takes steps to improve the experience for future batches.

WARNING: ICFAI Tech Hyderabad – A Factory, Not a University

If you’re considering joining ICFAI Tech Hyderabad, think again. This place parades as a university, but in reality, it’s a glorified high school with a college fee tag. The uniform compulsion here is just the tip of the iceberg  --  a reflection of the toxic, outdated, and control-obsessed mentality that governs this place.

Students are treated like children, not adults. You’re forced to wear uncomfortable, low-quality uniforms every day, regardless of the weather, occasion, or your comfort. It’s humiliating and dehumanizing  --  especially in an institution that claims to promote “freedom of thought” and “professional development.” Ironically, you’re expected to innovate while being suffocated under a one-size-fits-all policy.

What’s worse? The faculty and administration are more focused on enforcing dress codes than on improving the actual quality of education or listening to student concerns. You can get kicked out of class, fined, or even harassed by staff just because you dared to show up in your own clothes. It’s an environment built on fear, not learning.

This isn’t a university. It’s a discipline camp disguised as a college, where your individuality is erased and you’re expected to follow blindly. If you’re hoping for a healthy academic culture, supportive faculty, or even basic respect as a young adult  --  look elsewhere. There are far better institutions in India that treat their students with the maturity and dignity they deserve.

Don’t waste your time, money, or sanity. ICFAI Tech Hyderabad is not worth it.

One start rating is also not worth the college tbh.

The uniform rule at ICFAI Tech Hyderabad is absolutely ridiculous and completely unnecessary for a university -level institution. Instead of focusing on improving the quality of education, facilities, or placements, they are obsessed with enforcing outdated school-like dress codes. It feels like we are treated like school kids, not young adults preparing for the real world.

The uniforms are uncomfortable, low-quality, and completely impractical for Hyderabad's weather. Forget about expressing individuality or dressing appropriately for different activities like lab work, presentations, or casual classes. You are forced into the same bland, suffocating outfit every single day.

In a place that's supposed to nurture innovation, critical thinking, and independence, this kind of micromanagement is embarrassing. ICFAI needs to realize that professionalism comes from within, not from wearing the same ugly shirt and pants every day.

If you’re thinking of joining ICFAI Tech Hyderabad, just know you’re signing up for school 2.0  --  not a vibrant, mature university experience.

user_reviews.Name: Shubh
user_reviews.Description:
BITS Pilani is arguably India’s most prestigious private engineering and science university, often spoken of in the same breath as the IITs. What sets BITS apart is its unique "No Attendance Policy" and the "Practice School" (PS) program. The former fosters a sense of responsibility and self-discipline, while the latter integrates students into the industry for seven months, often leading to direct placements. The Pilani campus, located in the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan, is a sprawling, self-contained oasis known for its clock tower and the iconic Saraswati Temple.
Academically, BITS operates on a purely merit-based admission system through the BITSAT exam, which is notoriously competitive. The curriculum is flexible, allowing students to opt for "Dual Degrees," where they can combine a fundamental science degree with an engineering specialization. This interdisciplinary approach has created a powerful alumni network that dominates the global startup ecosystem; BITSians are known for founding more "unicorns" than almost any other Indian private institution.
Campus life at Pilani is intense and vibrant. From the cultural fest "Oasis" to the technical fest "APOGEE," the student-run nature of these events develops leadership skills. The residential requirement builds a lifelong brotherhood, and the "Redi" culture (small food kiosks) is where the real brainstorming happens. With its recent expansion into Goa, Hyderabad, and Dubai, BITS Pilani continues to redefine private higher education by maintaining the highest standards of academic integrity and innovation.

user_reviews.Name: Raj Kumar
user_reviews.Description:
Our experience with the BITSAT admission process was not very positive.

We are from Salem, Tamil Nadu. For national-level exams like JEE Main, exam centers are usually available in Salem itself, making it convenient for students. However, despite BITSAT being a computer-based online examination, we were allotted a test center in a college located on the outskirts of Coimbatore.

This required travel from Salem, along with transportation, food, and other expenses. The location had limited facilities nearby, making the experience inconvenient for both students and parents.

After spending considerable time and money for the first attempt, we decided to skip the second BITSAT attempt and instead focus our preparation on JEE Advanced. Looking back, that was the right decision for us.

Overall, we spent around ₹7,000 on the BITSAT application and related travel expenses. Had there been an exam center in Salem, like JEE Main provides, the experience would have been much easier and more student-friendly.

BITS Pilani is undoubtedly a reputed institution, but the lack of accessible exam centers for students from smaller cities created an unnecessary burden. Our experience with the examination process was disappointing, and we hope BITSAT expands its test center availability in future years.

Fortunately, our child was able to focus on other opportunities and secured admission through alternative pathways. However, our BITSAT experience remains a costly and frustrating one.

The University of Hyderabad (UoH), widely known as Hyderabad Central University (HCU), is one of India's premier postgraduate and research institutions. Recognized as an Institution of Eminence (IoE) by the Government of India, it is highly regarded for its rigorous academic environment, distinguished faculty, and lush, sprawling campus.
​Here is an overview of what makes the university stand out, along with some of its latest milestones.
​🏆 Recent Rankings & Global Recognition
​The university consistently secures top spots in national and international rankings, reflecting its strong research output and academic reputation.
​THE Asia University Rankings (2026): UoH retained its top slot among India's Central Universities, placing in the 251–300 bracket across Asia. The 2026 report specifically highlighted its high faculty-to-student ratio, significant PhD output, and heavy volume of publications in high-impact international journals.
​NIRF Rankings (2025):
​#18 in the University category.
​#26 in the Overall category.
​#32 in the Research Institutions category.
​🧬 Academic Excellence & Research Focus
​While UoH offers a wide array of multidisciplinary programs across the humanities, social sciences, and engineering, its science schools are particularly celebrated.
​The School of Life Sciences is a major driver of the university's global citation impact. Departments focusing on Plant Sciences, Biotechnology, and Bioinformatics are equipped with cutting-edge laboratories and foster an intense, research-driven culture. For graduates aiming to clear highly competitive national exams like the CSIR NET or those preparing to step into advanced PhD programs, the rigorous curriculum, hands-on molecular techniques, and strong peer environment at UoH provide a massive foundational advantage.
Campus Life & Bio-diversity
​Spread over 2,000 acres, the UoH campus is a serene oasis located in Gachibowli.
​A Green Haven: The campus is heavily forested and acts as a major bio-diversity hub, home to beautiful lakes, fascinating rock formations, and rich wildlife, including spotted deer, wild boars, and a vast variety of bird species.
​Vibrant Culture: It hosts a smorgasbord of cultures, with students from all over the country and the world. The student life is highly active, characterized by intellectual debates, cultural festivals, and political discussions at popular campus spots like "Shopcom."

The University of Hyderabad, often called "Gachibowli Central University," is a premier postgraduate and research institution. Located on a 2,300-acre campus filled with rock formations, lakes, and diverse flora and fauna, UoH offers one of the most beautiful and tranquil academic environments in India. It was established as a result of the "Six-Point Formula" of 1973 and has since become a top choice for students pursuing Master's and Doctoral studies.
UoH is renowned for its School of Physics and School of Chemistry, which are consistently ranked among the best in the country for research impact. The university’s "Integrated Masters" program is also highly sought after by high school graduates who want to dive straight into research. The academic culture here is highly decentralized and flexible, allowing students to take electives across different schools, fostering a truly interdisciplinary mindset.
The campus life is laid-back but intellectually charged. With no "gates" between hostels and a culture of 24/7 library access, students have the freedom to manage their own learning. The university is also a hub for social and political discourse, reflecting the diverse backgrounds of its students who come from every corner of India. For someone focused on a career in pure sciences, social sciences, or humanities research, UoH provides the perfect balance of academic freedom, high-quality faculty, and state-of-the-art laboratory facilities.

user_reviews.Description:
Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH) is one of India’s premier institutes of science and technology, established in 2008 as part of the IIT expansion to strengthen high-quality technical education and research. Located in Kandi, Sangareddy district of Telangana, IITH is known for its modern infrastructure, interdisciplinary culture, and strong emphasis on innovation-driven research.
IIT Hyderabad stands out among newer IITs for its early adoption of a fully residential, self-contained campus with state-of-the-art laboratories, smart classrooms, and advanced research facilities. The institute offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs across engineering, science, design, and liberal arts. Departments such as Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, and Mathematics have gained national and international recognition.
A defining feature of IITH is its strong research orientation. The institute actively collaborates with global universities, research labs, and industry partners. Areas like artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, cybersecurity, semiconductor technology, biomedical engineering, and computer vision -- including face recognition -- are key research strengths. Faculty members frequently publish in top-tier journals and conferences such as CVPR, ICCV, TPAMI, and IEEE transactions.
Innovation and entrepreneurship are deeply embedded in campus culture through the Technology Incubation and Entrepreneurship Cell (TIEC), which supports startups and translational research. Students are encouraged to work on real-world problems, participate in hackathons, and engage in interdisciplinary projects.
With a young, dynamic faculty, flexible academic structure, and a rapidly growing global reputation, IIT Hyderabad is emerging as a leading hub for advanced research, technological innovation, and academic excellence in India.

user_reviews.Description:
I would strongly advise not to blindly follow what people say. Many claim this is a “top college,” but in my opinion, it is one of the most overrated colleges in Hyderabad. Its reputation exists mainly because of what people say, not because of the actual experience.

The reality is quite different  --  the classrooms are not well maintained, the washrooms are in poor condition, and the overall infrastructure does not meet expectations. There is also a lack of proper placement training and student support.

If I start listing all the issues, there are many more. So please don’t rely only on public opinion  --  try to understand the ground reality before making a decision. Instead, consider exploring other universities like KL or GITAM or vnr vjit.
